notes: Identical to C1: the source fix is the same as the reference, with comprehensive tests that check refcount and file state through internal fields rather than end-to-end accept behaviour.
Identical to C1: the source matches the reference, and the solid but internals-coupled test suite does not verify that the remaining holder keeps accepting after a sibling close.

The source change matches the reference exactly: it closes and unlinks synchronously under the mutex, makes a double Close return ErrClosed via a CAS flag, guards abstract sockets, and closes the dup'd fd. The tests are thorough (refcount, double close, immediate unlink with refused dial, abstract sentinel, close/relisten race for both unix and unixgram), but they lean on internals like the deleteListener cast and count.Load, and never check that the remaining holder still accepts.

The source change is identical to the reference fix. The tests check behaviour through the public Listen API: the surviving holder still accepts after a sibling closes or double-closes, the race test uses a start barrier and also checks close errors and the final unlink, unixgram is covered with a datagram round trip plus double close, and the abstract-socket sentinel is covered; only a unixgram race case is missing.

Functionally correct, including single-file symlink roots, but squashfs uses a convoluted double-lookup with remote-string comparisons in New/NewObject, and zip Open gets an odd symlink-only offset special case; the tests are extensive, but the escape test does not assert that the copy fails.
Identical to C2: a reference-equivalent implementation plus docs and reasonable, if not exhaustive, tests.

Code matches the reference fix for both zip and squashfs, with a sensible docs section; the tests cover the skip/translate behaviour, the squashfs regular-suffix case and an end-to-end escape check, but omit range/seek and the zip regular-suffix NewObject case.

Meets the spec, but squashfs silently falls back to an empty link target if Readlink isn't available instead of erroring, and zip doesn't exclude directory entries from symlink detection; a binary squashfs fixture is added, though it lets the tests run without mksquashfs, and the tests and docs are otherwise good.

Solid implementation: squashfs does exact-name then suffix lookup, link targets are read robustly via Readlink or StatT, and roots naming a symlink (bare or suffixed) work in both backends; the withinRoot refactor adds some churn, and the tests are comprehensive.

Works and also handles a single-file symlink root, but the zip side reads every symlink member eagerly with an unbounded io.ReadAll inside readZip, which costs extra (remote) I/O and risks memory blowup at mount time, and squashfs reads --links from each call's ctx instead of the Fs; the tests are thorough (list/NewObject agreement, range/seek, regular .rclonelink file, copy, escape).
